plan.hypothesis: Projecting every channel of the plain SwinIR float32 prediction onto the closed valid RGB interval [0,1] will improve frozen Urban100-12 mean paired PSNR-Y by at least 0.05 dB versus the fixed two-pass horizontal-flip reference while keeping candidate/reference latency at or below 2.5 times.
plan.mechanism: The candidate applies the Euclidean projection onto the valid normalized RGB box independently at every sample. If the unknown reference RGB lies in [0,1]^3, replacing an out-of-range prediction by its nearest point in that convex box cannot increase continuous RGB squared distance to that reference; in-range predictions are unchanged. I infer that eliminating network overshoot may improve the evaluator's quantized luminance error, but the cited papers do not establish that it will beat the stronger two-pass reference, and the RGB projection argument does not itself guarantee PSNR-Y improvement after quantization.
plan.baseline: Comparator: the existing fixed two-pass SwinIR-S x2 horizontal-flip ensemble reference. Candidate path: one plain, unensembled fixed SwinIR-S x2 prediction followed only by per-channel clipping to [0,1]. The candidate neither calls the model nor obtains a second prediction.
plan.why_not_g1_retry: This is not a G1 retry: it uses one prediction and a convex range projection, not flip averaging or any prediction ensemble. It also does not use LR-versus-SR residual backprojection (G2); spatial-frequency attenuation, shrinkage, blur, or gating (G3); global luminance contrast expansion or its reversal (G4); luminance-preserving chroma gamut compression; phase-locked offset estimation/correction; or selection among 8-bit RGB lattice corners (G5). It does not retune or add complexity to any stopped route, including the local linux-g5-20261104 and linux-validation-20261104 routes.

new_evidence.claim: Takeyama, Ono, and Kumazawa formulate image restoration with a hard image dynamic-range constraint and implement that constraint through metric projection, explicitly giving componentwise clipping to the allowed interval.
new_evidence.why_distinct: This primary paper, outside the excluded evidence list, motivates feasible-set projection rather than ensembling, observation-residual correction, frequency shrinkage, contrast manipulation, chroma-only gamut compression, phase correction, or quantization-lattice selection. Applying that general constraint to RGB SISR is my inference, not a result claimed by the paper.

new_evidence.claim: Lim et al. report that direct RGB residual-network reconstruction is an effective formulation for single-image super-resolution and evaluate it on standard SR benchmarks.
new_evidence.why_distinct: This primary SR paper establishes the relevant direct-RGB prediction setting; it does not claim that post-hoc clipping beats an ensemble. The proposed feasible-range projection and its expected benefit are my inference.

controls: Twelve Urban100 x2 pairs selected by fixed study-id/filename hash excluding historical and local reserved IDs, before search; no image or score selection
Candidate: plain fixed SwinIR-S x2 prediction followed by one agent-authored deterministic array function
Comparator: existing fixed two-pass horizontal-flip SwinIR-S x2 reference; no optimization or reopening G1
CPU float32, four reference threads, same weights, official padding, RGB/uint8 conversion, Y metric, border crop 2
No training, extra weights, model forwards in candidate code, parameter sweeps, repeated holdout access, or automatic retries
All constants frozen in candidate.py and research.json before registration; synthetic checks only before registration
plan.stop_route: A valid negative eliminates fixed componentwise projection of plain SwinIR RGB output onto [0,1] as a route to beating the fixed two-pass reference under these gates; it does not isolate clipping causality from the single-versus-double-forward difference and will not justify changing bounds, using soft/adaptive clipping, or adding rescue complexity.

parameters.projection: componentwise np.clip on all RGB samples
parameters.rationale: The bounds are the declared normalized valid RGB domain, so they require no fitted strength or holdout-dependent choice; exact metric projection is deterministic and parameter-free.
